Judgment
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the death of Ankith Yadav in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
2.

That, on 11.04.2024 at about 3-00 p.m, the deceased Ankith Yadav was riding a Bullet motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-50-EK-6525 on Surdenapura-Adde Road, when he reached in front of Sharada Thapovana, Adde Village, Hesaraghatta Hobli, Yelahanka, Bengaluru at that time, a dog came infront of the said motorcycle.
Due to which, the deceased applied sudden brake and lost control over the same and dashed against the road side ditch wall.
Due to the tremendous impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that immediately after the accident, he was shifted to CRPF Camp Hospital, Bengaluru, first aid treatment, thereafter he was shifted to M.S Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was taken treatment as an inpatient and died in the said hospital during the course of treatment on 27.04.2024.
Thereafter post mortem was conducted and the deadbody was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.6,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 23 years and working as a Security Guard, at Rudra Corporate Services, Avalahalli and earning Rs.3,330/- per month and contributing the entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have put to untold misery, pain, shock and mental agony.
5. It is further stated that, the accident occurred due to the involvement of Bullet motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50-EK-6525.
Hence, jurisdictional Rajanakunte Police have filed criminal case in Cr.No.122/2024 against rider of said vehicle.
Hence, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.

sentences.text: In response to the notice, respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent, placed exparte.
7. In the written statement the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent No.2 has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of bike bearing registration No.KA-50-EK-6525 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is contended that the rider of insured vehicle is not a third party, hence the deceased who is rider of the insured vehicle cannot be treated as a third party.
Further contended that the rider of the vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of the accident.

Further contended that, neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
The respondent took specific contention that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Sri.Ankit Yadav died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 11-04-2024 at about 3:00 PM, in front of Sharada Thapovana, Surdenapura - Adde road, Adde village,
Hesaraghatta Hobli, Yelahanka, Benglauru due to the involvement of motorcyle bearing registration No.KA-50-EK-6525 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the deceased?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
4) What order or award?

9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.2 got examined herself as PW1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
10.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 examined its Authorized signatory as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
11.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel.
Perused the materials available on record.

sentences.text:
My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Affirmative Issue No.3: In the Negative Issue No.4: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1 & 2 :
13.
These two issues are taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts.

14. It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the accident, Ankit Yadav, Son of Sanjay Kumar was dead, while he was riding the offending vehicle, in unavoidable circumstance, as noted above.

15. According to the petitioners the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-50-EK-6525, was ridden by the deceased as on the date of the accident, while proceeding in the scene of occurrence, accident had taken place.
In the said accident son of the petitioner No.1 succumbed to the injuries.

The petitioners being the legal heirs of the deceased had filed the claim petition seeking compensation,
under section 164 of the M.V Act.
16.
It is pertinent to note that, present petition have been filed under section 164 of M.V. Act 1989.
As such, it is important to note the said provision.

(i) Not withstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of the motor vehicle.
17. On going through the aforesaid provision, I am of the view that, proof of actionable negligence is not required in connection with the present facts and circumstances of the case.
The present facts of the case, reflects that, the deceased himself was tortfeasor as on the date of the accident.
On going through the police papers along with the evidence of PW1 reveal that, first information about the accident was given by the petitioner No.2 against the rider of the offending vehicle.
In the recitals of the complaint marked at Ex.P2, there is a clear narration that, in the self accident Ankit Yadav had succumbed to the injuries.

On the basis of complaint given by PW1, the SHO of Rajanukunte police has registered case against the deceased Ankit Yadav, for the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
18.

Apart from this, spot mahazar and the spot sketch marked at Ex.P3 & Ex.P7 there is a clear narration that deceased dashed to wall of the drainage and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries in the hospital.
Ex.P4 is the IMV report reveals that, accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.

Ex.P5-Inquest report reveals that,
due to the accidental injuries Ankit yadav, son of the petitioner No.1 was dead.
Ex.P6 is the post mortem report goes to show that, the death was due to "septicemia as a result of injury to the left lower limb sustained".

Ex.P15 is the reply to the notice u/s 133 of MV act, reveals that during the Manju Devi vs Sanjay Kumar on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133850570/
4 course of investigation process, notice was issued to the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle by name Sanjay Kumar the respondent No.1 in the case on hand and Ankit Yadav was the rider of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
It is crystal clear from his reply that, at the time of accident, son of the petitioner No.1 was the rider of the offending vehicle.

19. Ultimately, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer as per Ex.P8 reveals that, charge sheet has been filed against Ankith Yadav on the allegation that, he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC and in column No.17 noted that, the accused/son of the petitioner No.1 died in the accident.
Ex.P9 to Ex.P11 are nothing but Aadhar cards of the petitioners and deceased which reveals the relationship between petitioners with the deceased.
The said relationship is not disputed point in issue, in the case on hand.

20. On appreciation of the evidence placed on record by the PW1, it is crystal clear that, the accident and death of the son of the petitioner No.1 and the brother of the PW1, is not disputed point in issue.
But the son of the petitioner No.1 himself was tortfeasor to the said accident.
The deceased himself was responsible for accident and its consequences.
21. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 placed the evidence of its official as RW1.

He has stated in his evidence that deceased Ankit himself was riding the bike bearing No.KA-50-EK-6525 and the deceased being the rider of the insured vehicle, cannot be considered as a third party to claim any sought of compensation.
The police after thorough investigation has filed the charge sheet against the deceased rider Ankit Yadav himself, the deceased being the tortfeasor.
Hence, the petitioners are not entitled for compensation.
22. At the time of cross-examination of PW1, she has stated that, at the time of accident her brother was riding the two wheeler.
The offending vehicle belonged to her father Sanjay Kumar and all the documents are standing in the name of the respondent No.1.
Further, she denied that her brother was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
In connection with the accident, she has given belated complaint after 17 days of the accident before the police.
Apart from this, some of the answers given by her during the course of cross- examination clearly depict that, her brother was tortfeasor.
Due to his negligence, accident and its consequences were taken place.
Some of the material answers elicited from her mouth is important to reproduce herein.
On perusal of the answers given by the PW1 and admission from her side reflects that, her brother himself was responsible for accident.
Hence, the petitioners through their evidence clearly established the fact of accident and death of Shri Ankit Yadav, in the said accident, due to his sole negligence.
As such, more discussions on other points is not required.
Hence, I am answering the issue No.1 & 2 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:

sentences.text: Now coming to the point of entitlement of relief sought for by the petitioners is concerned, question would arises, when the deceased himself was tortfeasor, whether his legal representative are entitled for compensation.
25. The learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners are seeking compensation under section 164 of M.V. Act for death of Ankit Yadav.
Further under section 164 of M.V. Act, the petitioners are not required to prove the negligent act of the rider.

Further learned counsel has relied the judgment passed in MVC No.6148/2022 dated 5.10.2023 by the IX Addl. Small Causes and Additional MACT,
Bengaluru.
I have gone through the said judgment, but the said judgment is not binding on this Tribunal.
26. Further, it is very settled position of law that, both the tortfeasor and the victim cannot be the same person.

At this stage, it is necessary rely the following decisions;
1) 2010 ACJ 1667, between Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited V/S. B.C Kumar and Another.
2) MFA No.6455/2014 between Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Madhu H.K.
27.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Madhu H.K.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the aforesaid cases, it was highlighted that, when the claimant himself being the tortfeasor,
question of considering his case for grant of compensation does not arise.
At the same time, the legal representatives of the tortfeasor are not entitle to get any compensation under law.
The material on record did point that the petitioner is not the owner of the motor cycle, his father is the R.C. owner.
Since the petitioner borrowed the motor cycle, he stepped into the shoes of the R.C. owner.

28. Apart from the above case, In Supreme Court Cases 2012(2) Page 356 between National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Sineetha, The Honourable Apex Court, while discussing the position of law with regard to section 147 and 149 of M.V. Act observed that, victim/deceased if third party or not,
relationship with owner need to aver, establish and through insurance company seeking to deny liability on the ground that, the driver of motor vehicle injured in accident was not a third party.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., vs. Sineetha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is essential for the insurer to establish that the driver having occupied shoes of owner cannot be treated as a third party - only factual details brought on record through reliable evidence can discharge the aforesaid onus.

Since, no relationship of driver was established with the owner nor capacity in which he was riding the vehicle had been brought out, it is not possible to conclude that rider while riding motor cycle on fateful day was an agent, employee or representative of owner.

29. In the light of my detailed discussion held above, no doubt the motor cycle in question belonged to the respondent No.1, the rider of the said vehicle as on the date of the said accident was the brother of PW1.
There is no evidence from the side of the PW1 that the deceased was riding the vehicle in question on the capacity of owner or borrower cum agent of the owner of the motor cycle.

As per the police papers and evidence of PW1 and admissions forthcoming in the cross-examination clearly evident that, the brother of PW1 himself was tortfeasor to cause accident, he being tortfeasor consequent upon the accident, succumbed to the death.

In such a situation, the petitioners cannot Manju Devi vs Sanjay Kumar on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133850570/
6 claim any compensation under the umbrella of beneficial legislation.

sentences.text: In the name of beneficial legislation Tribunal cannot grant compensation as a matter of right, in all the cases without looking at the ingredients of the provision under which the main petition filed for compensation.
30. Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioners have not made out sufficient grounds to claim compensation.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.3 in the Negative.

ISSUE No.4:
31.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 164 of MV Act, is hereby dismissed.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances, no order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
